solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: My career churning in butter factory

indicators.note: churning stirs things vigorously, so the letters get thoroughly mixed up

parts.note: the two words supply all eight letters

explanation.surface: Someone's working life is spent stirring cream at a dairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Churning' fits the butter picture so neatly that it hides its job as the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A creamery is a dairy establishment where cream is processed into butter and cheese.

clue.text: Island seabird seen below Cape reservoir?

indicators.note: in a down entry, being seen below something means coming after it in the grid

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for a cape
IS is a standard abbreviation for island
a tern is a gull-like seabird

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spots an island seabird beneath a headland near a reservoir.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: a tank of water is a small, domestic reservoir.
explanation.definitionFit: A cistern is a tank storing water, effectively a small household reservoir for supply.

clue.text: Insect leaving gnu, say, to run off

indicators.note: when something is leaving, it departs and is no longer part of the word

parts.note: a gnu is one example of this kind of animal, hence 'say'
the ant is a common insect

explanation.surface: An insect flees from a gnu on the savannah.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks gnu as an example of a wider class, so the solver must go up a level to the general animal before removing the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly, usually with a lover in order to marry.

clue.text: Skilful handling of rampant tulip mania working

indicators.note: rampant means running wild, so the letters break free of their order

parts.note: taken as written
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Someone deftly manages the frenzied seventeenth-century Dutch craze for tulip bulbs.
explanation.walkthrough: Tulip mania was the Dutch bulb-speculation bubble of the 1630s; 'working' adds two letters to the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Manipulation means deft control or treatment by hand, as a physiotherapist or puppeteer uses.

clue.text: Ruin regularly leads writer to mature

indicators.note: one part leading another means it comes first in the answer
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of that word is kept

parts.note: first and third letters of the word
a pen is a writing implement, a classic crossword writer

explanation.surface: A ruined author is somehow led towards maturity.
explanation.definitionFit: To ripen is to become fully developed, as fruit does when it grows ready to eat.

clue.text: Spot a line missing in voting paper

indicators.note: things that are missing have been taken out, leaving the rest behind

parts.note: a ballot is the paper on which a vote is cast
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: An election official notices a voting slip with a line left out.
explanation.definitionFit: A blot is a stain or mark, such as an ink splodge, so it is a spot.

clue.text: Missing being idle when son's away

indicators.note: someone away is absent, so that letter is not present in the word

parts.note: slacking is being lazy or idle
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent laments lazing about whenever their boy is out of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking means absent or wanting, so something lacking is not there at all.

clue.text: Commerce is traditional with English

indicators.note: with means alongside, so one piece is simply placed next to the other

parts.note: trad is the short informal form, as in trad jazz
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A claim that business in Britain is old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade is buying and selling goods, the activity that commerce names.

clue.text: Disorderly, hungover and unable? Off their heads

indicators.note: and simply joins the two trimmed words one after the other
with their heads off, both words lose their opening letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rowdy revellers, the morning after and incapable, described as off their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off their heads' reads as slang for drunk, fitting the hangover, but it instructs removing the first letter of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ungovernable cannot be controlled or ruled, which makes it unruly and disorderly.

clue.text: Promised the return of northern banks

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
banks of keys or seats are rows

explanation.surface: Someone vows that the riverbanks up north will come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' suggests rivers, but it means tiers or lines, as in a bank of switches.
explanation.definitionFit: Sworn means having made a solemn oath or pledge, so it means promised.

clue.text: Father's holding a winning card, which makes all well

indicators.note: the apostrophe-s stands for 'has', and having something held means wrapping round it

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for father
an is the indefinite article before a vowel
the ace is the top card in many games

explanation.surface: Dad has a trump card in hand that solves everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'a' gives the article in its form before a vowel. The definition is a descriptive phrase for a thing, read as 'something which makes all well'.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a supposed universal cure, a remedy that heals every ailment.

clue.text: Animal trapped in the well

indicators.note: something trapped in other words is enclosed within them, spanning the gap

parts.note: the letters sit across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A creature has fallen down a well and is stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe is a female sheep, a farm animal.

clue.text: Show changing time on map

indicators.note: changing means altering, so the order of the letters is altered

parts.note: the three words supply all nine letters

explanation.surface: A display that alters the hour shown on a map, like a time-zone chart.
explanation.walkthrough: A pantomime is a British Christmas stage show for families, full of slapstick and audience participation.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantomime is a theatrical entertainment, so it is a kind of stage show.

clue.text: Chap turned back before a place in Cambridgeshire specifically

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the second in the answer
turning back means facing the other way, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a chap is a man
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, an English county

explanation.surface: A man turns round before heading to a particular Cambridgeshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: Namely introduces an exact detail, meaning that is to say or in particular.

clue.text: Bend in river is more tight around delta

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: tight means stingy, so more tight is meaner
Delta is D in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A river grows narrower as it winds round its delta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' suggests a sharp curve in the river, but it means miserly.
explanation.definitionFit: A meander is a winding curve in the course of a river, named after a Turkish one.

clue.text: Down-and-out, mostly rough-edged bachelor returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the combined letters run backwards
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a ragged edge is rough and uneven
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in a BA degree

explanation.surface: A scruffy single man comes home, nearly destitute.
explanation.definitionFit: A beggar is a destitute person living on charity, which is what a down-and-out is.

clue.text: Quickly paid running into railway

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it

parts.note: RLY is the abbreviation for railway

indicators.note: running suggests things moving about, so the letters are set loose

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who was quickly paid runs into a railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapidly is an adverb meaning at speed, the same sense as quickly.

clue.text: Try and move round to hide key symptom of indigestion

parts.note: to try a case in court is to hear it

indicators.note: to hide something is to cover it up, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to turn is to rotate or move round
B is a musical key

explanation.surface: Instructions for searching: attempt it, then rotate something to conceal a key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is the judicial sense: a judge tries, or hears, a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartburn is the burning chest pain from stomach acid, a classic sign of indigestion.

clue.text: Drag bundles of corn endlessly

indicators.note: without ends means both the first and last letters are cut off

parts.note: sheaves are bound bundles of cut corn stalks

explanation.surface: A farmhand hauls bundles of harvested corn on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to haul or pull with great effort, which is what dragging something involves.

clue.text: Distressed to go down after being at university

indicators.note: after places this piece behind the earlier one in the answer

parts.note: a student at university is said to be up, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
the sun sets when it goes down

explanation.surface: A student is unhappy about leaving university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go down' is also British slang for leaving university, which makes the surface coherent.
explanation.definitionFit: Upset is an adjective meaning unhappy or troubled, the same as distressed.

clue.text: Be unsuccessful getting rid of large peacock

indicators.note: getting rid of something means throwing it out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to flop is to fail
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A failed attempt to get rid of a big bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peacock' looks like the bird, but here it is a vain, showy man.
explanation.definitionFit: A fop is a man excessively concerned with his dress, figuratively a vain strutting peacock.

clue.text: Country abandoning European currency

indicators.note: abandoning something means leaving it behind, so that letter goes

parts.note: France is a country
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A nation drops the shared European money.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls France giving up its own money for the euro, which makes the answer neatly ironic.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was France's monetary unit before the euro and remains Switzerland's money.

clue.text: A right pair mostly exercise hard

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
a duo is a pair
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: Two people working out together find it tough going.
explanation.definitionFit: Arduous describes a task needing great effort and endurance, so it is difficult.

clue.text: British countryside is rather insipid

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
land is the countryside, as in working the land

explanation.surface: A grumble that the British countryside is a bit dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Bland means lacking flavour or interest, a mild version of tasteless and dull.

clue.text: Merit attention before the third of June

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the next

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention

indicators.note: only the letter in position three of that word is taken

parts.note: the third letter of the month's name

explanation.surface: Someone deserves notice ahead of a date early in summer.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn something is to deserve it through effort, which is what meriting it means.

clue.text: End of stay after prison sentence able to be lengthened

indicators.note: after places this piece behind the following one in the answer

parts.note: a stretch is slang for a term in prison

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A prisoner's stay ends after a sentence that keeps being extended.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stretchy is elastic, so it can be pulled out longer.
